section: Attention Is all you need research paper transformation

content: The paper introduces the Transformer, a new neural network architecture designed mainly for sequence-to-sequence tasks such as machine translation. Unlike traditional models that depend on recurrent neural networks (RNNs) or convolutional neural networks (CNNs), the Transformer uses attention mechanisms alone. This removes the need for sequential computation, allowing the model to process many parts of a sequence in parallel. The paper shows that the Transformer achieves better translation quality while requiring significantly less training time.

Before the Transformer, sequence-processing tasks commonly used RNNs, LSTMs, and GRUs. These models process words one after another, which makes parallel processing difficult and increases training time, especially for long sequences. Attention mechanisms were already being used to help models understand relationships between words, but they were generally combined with recurrent networks. The Transformer was proposed to remove this sequential dependency and use self-attention to directly connect different positions in a sequence. This makes it easier to learn long-distance relationships and allows much greater parallelization.

The Transformer follows an encoder-decoder architecture consisting entirely of attention-based components. It has 6 identical encoder layers and 6 identical decoder layers. Each encoder layer contains multi-head self-attention followed by a feed-forward neural network, with residual connections and layer normalization. The decoder contains these components plus an additional encoder-decoder attention layer. The decoder also uses masked self-attention so that it cannot look at future output words.

The input and output tokens are converted into embeddings, and positional encoding is added so the model can understand the order of words. The main attention mechanism is Scaled Dot-Product Attention, while Multi-Head Attention allows the model to focus on different relationships between words simultaneously. The original Transformer uses 8 attention heads. 

After transforming the fifa dataset with attention is all you need

The “Attention Is All You Need” paper introduces the Transformer architecture, originally designed for sequence-to-sequence tasks such as machine translation. Unlike traditional RNN- and CNN-based models, the Transformer relies mainly on self-attention and multi-head attention, allowing the model to process different elements in parallel and capture relationships between distant elements.

The FIFA dataset is tabular rather than sequential text and contains various numerical and categorical player-related features. To apply the Transformer concept, each feature can be represented as a token or embedding instead of treating words as tokens. This allows the model to learn relationships between different player attributes.

For the FIFA application, the original encoder-decoder structure can be simplified to an encoder-based architecture with a prediction head, since the objective is to predict a value or class rather than generate a sequence. The features are first converted into embeddings along with information about their feature identity, and then passed through the Transformer encoder. The original Transformer encoder consists of multi-head self-attention, feed-forward networks, residual connections, and layer normalization.

The multi-head self-attention mechanism is the key component because it enables the model to learn interactions between different FIFA features. For example, it can potentially learn relationships between goals and shots, assists and passing statistics, or stamina and distance covered. Multiple attention heads can examine different relationships simultaneously.

After the encoder processes the features, their representations are aggregated into a single representation and passed to a prediction head. The prediction head can then produce an output such as a player rating, performance score, or classification result. Therefore, the overall architecture can be represented as:
FIFA Dataset → Feature Embedding → Feature/Column Information → Transformer Encoder → Multi-Head Self-Attention → Feed-Forward Network → Aggregation → Prediction Head → Final Prediction

This adaptation allows us to use the main advantage of the Transformer—learning complex relationships between input elements through attention—for FIFA tabular data rather than using it only for natural-language sequences.

The process starts with the FIFA player dataset, which contains numerical features such as age, goals, assists, stamina, and pass accuracy, along with categorical features such as position, team, and nationality. The data is first processed by handling missing values, normalizing numerical features, and encoding categorical features so that it can be used by the model.

Next, the processed features are converted into feature embeddings or tokens. Numerical features are transformed into dense vectors, while categorical features use learned embeddings. A feature/column identity embedding is also added so the model knows which token represents each attribute, such as goals, stamina, or position.

These feature tokens are then passed through the Transformer Encoder, which contains multi-head self-attention, feed-forward networks, residual connections, and layer normalization. Self-attention allows the model to learn relationships between different FIFA attributes, such as goals and shots, assists and passing, or stamina and distance covered. Multiple attention heads allow different types of feature relationships to be learned simultaneously.

Finally, the encoder outputs are aggregated into a single player representation and passed to a prediction head. The model can then produce outputs such as a predicted player rating or performance category. Thus, the overall flow is:
FIFA Dataset → Feature Processing → Embeddings → Transformer Encoder → Self-Attention → Aggregation → Prediction → Player Performance.

section: Why Do We Need This Process?
Why Do We Need This Process?
content: The main reason for adapting the Transformer to the FIFA dataset is to capture complex relationships between different features. A football player's performance is influenced by multiple attributes rather than a single statistic. For example, goals may be related to shots and shots on target, while passing performance may be related to successful passes, pass accuracy, and creativity. A Transformer-based approach allows these relationships to be learned through self-attention rather than considering every feature independently.

section: Why Do We Need This Process?
content: Another important reason is the ability of self-attention to establish direct relationships between different elements. The original paper explains that self-attention connects different positions with a constant number of sequential operations, making long-range dependencies easier to learn compared with recurrent architectures. When this idea is transferred to tabular FIFA data, the different columns can interact with one another through attention, allowing the model to learn higher-level feature interactions.

section: What Do We Gain From This?
What Do We Gain From This?
content: The main benefit is the possibility of achieving better predictive performance by learning complex feature interactions. Instead of manually deciding which FIFA statistics are important or creating many combinations of features ourselves, the attention mechanism can learn useful relationships during training. Multi-head attention also provides multiple representation spaces through which different relationships can be learned. The original paper notes that different attention heads can learn different behaviors related to the structure of the input.

section: What Do We Gain From This?
content: Another advantage is parallel processing. Traditional recurrent models process sequence elements sequentially, which limits parallelization. The Transformer was specifically introduced to overcome this limitation and enable substantially greater parallelization. Although the FIFA dataset is tabular rather than sequential text, the same attention mechanism allows the feature representations to be processed together rather than forcing the model to process the features one after another.

section: What Do We Gain From This?
content: Overall, the purpose of this project is not to reproduce the original Transformer exactly, but to adapt its central idea—self-attention—to FIFA tabular data. The original paper provides the foundation, while the FIFA dataset provides a different type of input and prediction problem. The resulting Table-Transformer uses the Transformer encoder to learn relationships between FIFA features and then uses a prediction head to produce the required output. This makes the project a practical application of the Transformer concept beyond its original natural-language-processing setting
